Verify rewrite DATA ONLY. Do not write improved examples or solve the user's task.
Read every input and target in full. Return one review per exact id and row_sha256.
input_verdict checks plausible natural drafts or dictation, recoverable intent, contradictions,
fake noise, padding and leaked authoring instructions. output_verdict checks natural appropriate
language and formatting. pair_verdict checks ALL facts, uncertainty, conditions, negation,
quantities, names, quotations, literals, requests versus assertions, and the supplied mode.
/transcribe permits punctuation, true disfluency removal and explicit corrections, not lexical
paraphrasing. Preserve meaningful words like German 'um' and 'er', colloquial Portuguese and
unfinished thoughts. /slack is casual minimal cleanup; a long input may be a pasted thread.
/prompt reorganizes a self-contained request and never answers it. It must not drop supplied
material, hedges or constraints. /polish improves prose without omissions or changed certainty.
Identity inputs must remain byte-identical. Apply only supplied dictionary/profile context.
Check long texts paragraph by paragraph. Fail concrete defects. Uncertain means not confidently
justifiable. Pass requires no material defect. Overall verdict is fail if any dimension fails,
uncertain if any dimension is uncertain and none fails, otherwise pass. Give a concrete critique
for EVERY pair, citing the changed detail for defects. These are model judgments, not human labels.

Eli: The backing fabric has three small areas of thinning around the center seam. I marked their locations on the diagram, using the lettering panel as the reference point.

Priya: The fringe measures between 11 and 13 centimeters across the lower edge. A few ends are tangled, though I haven’t separated or trimmed any of them.

Eli: I found the inventory card in the gray folder. It calls the piece a “procession banner,” but it doesn’t give a maker or an exact date.

Mara: The card also lists a storage tube from the east cabinet. I checked that shelf this morning; the tube is there, with its paper label facing outward.

Priya: The banner itself is 86 centimeters wide at the top and 79 at the bottom. That difference may relate to the uneven edge, so I’ve written down both measurements.

Eli: I’ll compare those numbers with the older condition sheet after lunch. That sheet is dated 2008, and the measurements are written in pencil on the back page.

Mara: Quick note for the team: the small paper tag attached to the lining says “Room 4, case B.” I photographed it in place before recording the wording.

Jon: The tag is sewn through the lining, not the silk face. There’s a loose corner, but I haven’t lifted it to check what’s underneath.

Priya: 1. Surface and supports: the face is on the padded table; the lettering panel is supported; dust is visible at the top hem; the fringe remains untouched.

Eli: 2. Condition notes: the lower-right tear measures about 3.5 centimeters; the backing is thin at three points near the center seam; the top fold is darker than the surrounding silk.

Mara: 3. Records: the front, back, border, tear, and paper tag are photographed. The inventory card and the 2008 sheet are both in the gray folder for comparison.

Jon: I used the color card beside the border in two shots. In the third image, it was too close to the fringe, so I moved it and took another one.

Priya: The replacement image is in the folder now. The older shot is still there, labeled “color card near fringe,” so the sequence stays clear.

Eli: The table pad is clean, and I checked underneath it for loose thread before setting the banner down. I didn’t find any debris on the pale cover.

Mara: I’ll update the room log at noon and again before we leave. If the west sensor continues to lag, I’ll note the reading and the time the door was last opened.

Jon: I’ve put a small sign on the door asking people to keep it closed while they’re in the room. The hallway delivery cart is scheduled for 10:30.

Priya: I’ll be here when the cart comes through. The route can stay clear if we move the empty box beside the sink first; it isn’t holding any materials.

Eli: I’m labeling the diagram with the front-facing orientation and the banner’s top edge. That should make the tear and thinning marks easier to match to the photographs.

Priya — 6:48 am: I ran past at 6:10 and there was orange mesh across the entrance, no sign that I could read from the sidewalk. The north trailhead is open, but it adds about 1.4 miles to the loop.

Maya — 6:51 am: yep, creek gate. I didn’t see a posted notice either. Three newer runners were waiting by the bus stop and one left when nobody knew where to go. Can someone help me check the alternate route today?

Ben — 6:55 am: I can check after work, around 5:30. The map in our club folder is old though; it still shows the footbridge by the soccer fields, which was closed last winter after the railing got loose.

Rosa — 6:58 am: i have the updated county map saved. Footbridge is marked closed through June, and the gravel service lane behind the tennis courts is not a public path, even if it looks like a shortcut.

Dev — 7:03 am: good catch. For saturday we could meet at the library instead, then take Willow Ave to the north trailhead. Sidewalk is narrow for a big group, but there’s a crossing signal at 8th.

Maya — 7:07 am: library lot might work, but the farmers market sets up there at 7 and the east half fills fast. I can ask the library desk if club parking is okay before their doors open.

Omar — 7:12 am: I’m nearby now. Library lot has cones over 12 spaces and a market van unloading; there are still maybe 20 spaces on the west side. No paper notice about other events.

Nina — 7:16 am: could we move the start to the school lot on Juniper? It’s 0.6 miles from the trail entrance and has bathrooms. We’d need permission, though, and I don’t know who handles weekend access.

Leo — 7:20 am: I emailed the school office last fall about using that lot for the food drive. The auto reply says the office is closed on weekends; it doesn’t say whether the gate stays unlocked.

Priya — 7:24 am: also, the north entrance has a water fountain but it’s been turned off before April in past years. I can bring two refill jugs, though they only fit in my hatchback if I fold one seat down.

Ben — 7:29 am: I’ll bring my wagon for the jugs and first-aid kit. Does anyone know if the new route has a place for the 9:00 beginners group to wait without blocking the bike lane?

Maya — 7:34 am: quick route notes from yesterday’s walk, please flag anything I missed:
1) library to 8th Street crossing is about 0.3 mile, mostly flat, but the curb ramp on the south side is cracked.
2) 8th to Willow Ave has a narrow sidewalk for one block; runners should stay single file there.
3) north trailhead has a gravel lot, two benches, and a map board, but no reliable water or toilets.
4) from the trailhead we can use the yellow loop for 3 miles; the blue spur is muddy near the drainage ditch, so skip that one for now.

Rosa — 7:39 am: I walked the yellow loop Tuesday. The first half is packed dirt and the last quarter mile has loose stones; my ankle was fine in road shoes, but it’s rougher than the old creek path.

Dev — 7:43 am: thanks. We usually have 18 to 25 people, with two dogs some weeks. If we take the sidewalk in a single group, we’ll stretch past the signal. Maybe split by pace before leaving the library?

Maya — 7:47 am: yeah, that’s probably safer. I can bring the pace cards, but our laminated set is missing the 11-minute one. Is anyone able to print a replacement before friday?

Nina — 7:52 am: i can print it at home. Also, I have six reflective vests in my car, but the elastic on two is stretched out. I’ll bring all six and mark the bad ones with tape.

Omar — 7:58 am: one more thing: the route crosses the bike lane at Willow, and traffic was pretty quick at 6:30 today. A volunteer at the front and back could help, but we shouldn’t stop runners in the lane.

Leo — 8:04 am: agreed. I can be rear sweeper for the easy group. I’ve got a whistle, but the battery light on my headlamp is unreliable, so I’ll bring my spare clip light instead.

Priya — 8:10 am: I’m happy to lead the steady group if we keep the pace around 10:30 to 11:00. I can’t stay after 9:15, and I don’t want anyone assuming I’m available to drive people home.

Ben — 8:15 am: understood, no ride promises. I can lead the faster group and wait at the trailhead for the second group before we start the loop. My knee is okay for 3 miles, not the extra spur.

Maya — 8:21 am: we should also message the people who aren’t in this channel. Last week’s signup sheet has 31 names, but some only come once a month; can someone draft a short update that doesn’t sound like the gate is permanently closed?

Rosa — 8:26 am: I’ll write it. We should say the east gate is locked today, the county notice we saw said work begins monday, and we’re checking the alternate meetup. That leaves room for the schedule to change.

Dev — 8:31 am: I can check the county site at lunch and call the trail office if there’s a number listed. If the route status is unclear, I’d rather we use the park perimeter path than guess about access.

Maya — 8:37 am: good. Can two people help with the Saturday check? We need someone to confirm library parking and someone to walk the crossing and trail entrance around 7:15. Please reply here if you can.

Omar — 8:41 am: I can do the crossing check at 7:15. I’ll take a photo of the curb ramp and the map board, but I won’t post pictures of any runners without asking first.

Nina — 8:46 am: I can call the library today. If they say no parking, I’ll ask whether the market has a designated overflow lot nearby; I don’t want to promise the school lot until we hear back.

Leo — 8:51 am: can we keep the regular 6:30 start time for now? Some folks take the bus and plan around it. We can send the update tonight, then send a correction if the parking answer changes.

Maya — 8:56 am: yes, keep 6:30 for now and meet at the library west side unless Nina hears otherwise.
